To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have found a new class of Majorana bound states, the RSOC induced MBS at the junction interface between a topologically-trival superconductor and a normal metal, and that we have proposed a MBS-plus-Half Flux Quantum Vortex qubit platform for demonstrating non-abelian exchange statistics and for realizing topological quantum computing.

(1) we have identified the key conditions for the successful search for Majorana bound states in ramp-type Josephson junctions; (2) we have found evidence for MBS in d-wave superconducting ramp-type Josephson heterojunctions; and (3) we have designed a pi-loop Josephson heterojuctioin as a topologically protected qubit platform.
the Majorana fermions can be realized in a d-wave superconductive heterostructure, and the Majorana bound state plus half quantum vortex qubit platform is proposed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
exploring novel topological quantum phases and Majorana bound states, and their possible applications for quantum computing.
the development of new hybrid materials and structures that are capable of hosting MBS and topologically-protected qubits.
the development of novel hybrid superconductor based devices and heterostructures for probing the exotic quantum phenomena associated with Majorana fermions.

Majorana fermions are likely to be formed in d-wave superconductors.

Majorana bound states are indeed present in d-wave superconductors and that the proposed junction system and pi-loop heterostructures are the most promising platforms for realizing Majorana bound state based topological quantum computing devices.

the MBS in the d-wave superconductors are more accessible than the MBS in s-wave superconductors, and the MBS in d-wave superconducting heterostructure is more promising for topological quantum computation than MBS in s wave superconducting heterojunction.

the search for MBS in high-Tc junctions is a very promising direction.
